chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Huzayl ibn Hayyan, the brother of Ja'far ibn Hayyan Al-Sayrafi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I handed over some wealth to my brother Ja'far, so he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj from it, and I give in charity. I had asked those around us, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not permissible, and I would love to reach your verdict.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Did it reach you before you handed over your wealth to him?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So take from it what he gives to you, eat from it, drink, perform Hajj, and give in charity. So when you arrive in Iraq, say, Ja'far ibn Muhammad gave this verdict to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a creditor giving money to a debtor to spend on his behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* resolves a juristic dispute regarding *hiwalah* (debt transfer) or gifting by clarifying that if the creditor already possessed the funds before entrusting them to the debtor, the arrangement is valid (*sahih*) rather than invalid (*fasad*). The Imam’s instruction to cite his name upon returning to Iraq underscores the authority of his specific legal reasoning in distinguishing between mere possession and the transfer of ownership rights in financial transactions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Huzayl Bin Hayyan a brother of Ja’far Bin Hayyan Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I handed over some wealth to my brother Ja’far, so he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj from it, and I give in charity, and I had asked those around us, so they mentioned that, that is invalid and not Permissible, and I would love to end it to your<sup>asws</sup> words’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me ‘Did you receive it before you handed over your wealth to him’. I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘So take from it what he gives to you, and eat from it, and drink, and perform Hajj, and give in charity. So when you proceed to Al-Iraq, so say, ‘Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> gave this Verdict to me’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from Hudhayl ibn Hayyan, brother of Ja’far ibn Hayyan al-Sayrafiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I have given a certain amount of assets to my brother Ja’far and he gives me what I pay for my expenses, for performing al-Hajj and giving charity. I asked certain people for both of us and they mentioned that it is invalid and unlawful. I like to take your words as the final ones.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Did he give you such things before you gave him the assets you just mentioned?’ I replied, ‘Yes, he did so.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘You can take what he gives you, use it for food, drink, al-Hajj and charity, and when you go back to Iraq tell him that Ja’far ibn Muhammad has given me this fatwa.’”
